clue.text: Records a pound, extraordinary sum

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight, from Latin libra

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the usual order, so the letters of sum are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes down a remarkable sum of money paid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' reads as praise for the sum but is the anagram signal on the word sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Albums are collections of recorded music, so records in the sense of discs.

clue.text: Sharpness shown by a copper on it close to motorway

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the final letter of motorway is taken

explanation.surface: A policeman shows keen eyesight beside a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' gives the last letter of motorway; 'shown by' and 'on' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is keenness of sight or thought, a synonym for sharpness.

clue.text: Almost ring De Vere relaxing in pavilion

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym for ring is dropped

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell; a bell is a ring

indicators.note: relaxing suggests loosening the order, so the letters of De Vere are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named De Vere is unwinding in a pavilion while a phone almost rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts BELL to BEL; 'relaxing' turns DEVERE into VEDERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a summerhouse or gazebo built to command a view, a kind of pavilion.

clue.text: Wild animal gets Laurel in the face

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another, the comedian's name inside the word for face

parts.note: mug is slang for the face
Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A wild beast gets a laurel wreath thrust in its face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' looks like the plant but is the comedian; 'gets' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a feral horse of the American plains, an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Mysterious European, very tense man

parts.note: so can mean very, as in so tired
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A tense, enigmatic European man is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a few initiates, hence obscure or mysterious.

clue.text: Appears with good sort of act attracting prolonged applause

parts.note: shows means turns up or appears
topper is old British slang for a good fellow or a decent sort

explanation.surface: A performer appears with a good sort of act that wins a long ovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good sort' is dated British slang: a topper is a fine, decent person. 'with' and 'of' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A showstopper is a performance so well received that the applause halts the show.

clue.text: Husbandry prior to decline

parts.note: till means until, that is up to or prior to a time
to age is to grow old and decline

explanation.surface: Farming before falling into decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the cultivation of land, part of husbandry in the farming sense.

clue.text: Composer in rage over ending in 'Parsifal'

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed on top of, so the rage word sits above the next letter

parts.note: to rave is to rage wildly

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter, here of Parsifal

explanation.surface: A composer flies into a rage over the finale of Wagner's opera Parsifal.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, best known for Bolero.

clue.text: Worn, strangely, during visit in part of England

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the anagram goes inside the word for visit

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters of worn are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone looking worn out during a trip in an English region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns WORN into ORNW, which goes 'during' CALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip.

clue.text: What winter in Lapland is like? Head off, if not

indicators.note: taking off the head means dropping the first letter

parts.words: What winter in Lapland is like
parts.note: in the Arctic winter the sun barely rises, so the days are without sun

explanation.surface: A question about Lapland's dark winter, then a curt 'off with his head' condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Above the Arctic Circle the winter is lightless; 'Head off' removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless is a conjunction meaning except on condition that, i.e. if not.

clue.text: Completely astonish toxopholite?

definitions.meaning: to bowl someone over is to amaze or overwhelm them
a toxophilite is an archer, someone fond of the bow; read as two words a lover of bows

explanation.surface: An archer is utterly amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the phrase as a lover of the bow. The clue prints toxopholite for toxophilite.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings fit: the idiom for amaze, and a punning description of an archery enthusiast.

clue.text: Ambassador's enthralled by sign in reference book

indicators.note: being enthralled means held captive, so the ambassador piece is held inside the sign

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador; with the 's it gives HES

explanation.surface: A diplomat is captivated by a star sign found in a reference work.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the formal title of an ambassador; 'enthralled' disguises the containment as rapt attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing synonyms.

clue.text: Reptile unnerves nude no doubt, at first

parts.note: to rattle someone is to unnerve them

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is removed from the word for nude

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of doubt

explanation.surface: A snake unsettles a naked person, unsurprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no doubt, at first' means without D, the first letter of doubt, so NAKED becomes NAKE. 'no doubt' looks like a filler phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is a venomous American pit viper, an example of a reptile.

clue.text: Admit juvenile's lost face

indicators.note: losing its face means the word loses its front letter

parts.note: callow means immature or juvenile; the 's reads as has

explanation.surface: A youngster is humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost face' looks like an idiom for humiliation; here it removes the first letter of CALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow someone in is to admit them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A dance could make a number, not all, feel giddy

parts.note: eight is a number
some means a part, not all
to reel is to feel dizzy or giddy

explanation.surface: A dance that leaves several of the dancers dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome reel is a lively Scottish country dance for eight people.

clue.text: What may help to make jockeys relaxed?

definitions.text: What may help to make jockeys
definitions.meaning: ..., soft-ish ground conditions on a racecourse, makes riding easier for jockeys

explanation.surface: A question about what puts jockeys at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: Going is racing's term for the state of the turf; easy going means favourable conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Easygoing describes a calm, tolerant temperament, a synonym for relaxed.

clue.text: Yokel eating first piece of high game bird

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the letter goes within the word for yokel

parts.note: a yokel is a country bumpkin or peasant

indicators.note: the first piece of a word is its first letter, here of high

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin dines on well-hung game.
explanation.walkthrough: High game is meat hung until strongly flavoured, which disguises 'high' as part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed bird shot for sport, a classic game bird.

clue.text: Symbols and holy ciphers GI decoded

indicators.note: decoding a cipher rearranges it into sense, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A soldier cracks sacred codes written in symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieroglyphics are the pictorial characters of ancient Egyptian writing, a set of symbols.

clue.text: Character in love with Rosalind in Woolf novel

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's As You Like It the hero who woos Rosalind in the Forest of Arden
Virginia Woolf's 1928 novel about a gender-changing, centuries-long life

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean lover who also gives his name to a modern novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the hero of As You Like It and to the title of Woolf's novel.

clue.text: Anthem's opening before it

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: an intro is an opening or introduction

explanation.surface: A hymn's opening comes before the rest of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or anthem sung as the priest approaches the altar.

clue.text: What could be the beginning or be my undoing?

indicators.note: undoing means taking apart, so the letters of or be my are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether something will be a fresh start or their ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoing' looks like ruin but rearranges ORBEMY.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an organism at its earliest stage, the beginning of a life.

clue.text: Dismay a missionary, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the phrase is matched by its sound

parts.note: Saint Paul was the great missionary of the early church

explanation.surface: A missionary causes dismay, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror or dismay.

clue.text: Game — fine cuts for each

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the word for fine goes inside the word for each

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
OK means fine or acceptable

explanation.surface: A game where a fine cuts into each player's winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game played for stakes.

clue.text: Trick may get huge flans recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: mega is slang for huge
tarts are flans, open pastry cases

explanation.surface: A trick may bring enormous pastries back to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or ruse, a trick.

clue.text: State in a right state

parts.note: Kansas is a US state

explanation.surface: Someone is in quite a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a right state' reads as a British idiom for being agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a state of the southern US.

clue.text: Or is he mistaken, this shopkeeper?

indicators.note: mistaken means got wrong, so the letters of or is he are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a shopkeeper has been wrongly identified.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosier is a shopkeeper who sells stockings and socks.

clue.text: Go with extra pie

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in your turn
over means extra, left over

explanation.surface: Have a second helping of pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a pastry folded over a filling, a kind of small pie.

clue.text: Barking dogs at party

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of dogs at are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dogs make noise at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' (British slang for mad) rearranges DOGSAT. A stag do is a British pre-wedding party for the groom.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag do is a party held for a man before his wedding.
